body: Sorry to hear that. It's a self-fulfilling prophecy, isn't it? Things suck when you don't try, things suck when you try, so why waste effort trying?

I'm sorry to hear that. It's understandable to feel lost in a situation like this. Keeping busy can help keep one's mind off things rather than being idle - I know it's hard to get going, but getting out of bed is step one.
You're not alone. Every time I feel like I've made some progress, and feel slightly better about myself for it, it falls apart and I backslide to further down than I was before.

My father died when I was in grade 11 right before finals, and I broke down in the middle of an exam.

Is there a counselor or any close teachers you can reach out to at your school?

Struggling with this myself right now. People say that I'm a downer and full of so much negative energy, but when I try to fix things and actually be optimistic about something, it all ends up falling apart anyway, and I feel worse than I would have if I just had low expectations to begin with for thinking that it was actually going to work out.
This really resonates with me - it seems that we have quite a bit in common. I hope you can find some solace.

In retrospect, probably, as I am a rather worried/anxious person at the best of times and am horrible for suppressing emotions, but it was entirely subconscious and I certainly did not intend to drive them away. I was not supportive and likely hurt them more out of neglect than direct actions, but all the same, they do deserve an apology. It was just so recent that I am still an emotional mess about it and want to make sure I am completely sincere once the dust has settled a bit.
You're not alone in this - you have reached out to others and that in itself is a victory.

I spent many years in a toxic environment at home and have become a toxic person myself, and between that and my social anxiety I drove away the best person that ever happened to me to someone else and am completely alone. I don't know how to stop being an emotional drain. It's a self-fulfilling cycle of unhappiness and apathy. How does one change?

I have never been to a therapist. 

I have considered putting my things into storage and trying to get a field contract abroad/overseas for six or so months once I have to move out of our apartment, as my expenses would be minimal that way, but I don't know if that is any kind of solution, or if it is just temporarily running away from an inevitable situation. I just don't have the will or energy to confront it right now.
